newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir leader escapes grenade attack at rally.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir leader escapes grenade attack at rally.

text.p: Kashmir leader Farooq Abdullah escaped unhurt when suspected separatist guerrillas exploded a hand grenade and wounded 15 people at an election rally on Monday, police said.

They said the attack on Abdullah, the second in 11 days, took place at Kishtwar, some 240 km (150 miles) east of Jammu, winter capital of the troubled state of Jammu and Kashmir, where local elections are being held after a gap of nine years.
Abdullah escaped a similar grenade attack which wounded six people on September 12 at a village near Srinagar, the state's summer capital.
Police said that in Monday's attack the grenade exploded before it could be hurled into the area where Abdullah was speaking. Three of the wounded were in serious condition, they said.
The United News of India (UNI) said one person was killed, but this could not be immediately confirmed. UNI said the grenade exploded in the hands of a guerrilla who was himself injured.

Abdullah heads the National Conference party which is widely expected to win the four-stage polls scheduled to end on September 30. He was the chief minister when a separatist revolt broke out in 1990, giving way to direct federal rule.

Kashmiris voted on September 7, 16 and 21 amid tight security. More than 20,000 people have been killed during the separatist revolt in the troubled Himalayan region, India's only Moslem-majority state.
